Interesting! When I clicked the green at (19, 42) which is tile (2,6), the gray cross appeared at (30, 42) which is in the bottom section! Let me figure out the tile coordinates.
The gray cross center is at ~(30, 42). The bottom section starts at row 30. Let me check:
- Bottom section tile rows:
  - Row 1: 30-33
  - Row 2: 36-39
  - Row 3: 42-45
  - Row 4: 48-51
- Bottom section tile cols:
  - Col 1: 35-38
  - Col 2: 41-44
  - Col 3: 47-50
So the gray at ~(30, 42) is in the bottom section, tile row 1, col 2. That's tile (1,2) in the bottom section.
The green at (19, 42) is in the top section, tile (2,6). The gray appeared 2 tiles... but where? 
Wait, let me think about this differently. The top section has 3 rows and 7 columns. The bottom section has 4 rows and 3 columns. They share the same rightmost columns (41-50).
The green at (2,6) in the top section is at the rightmost column of the top section. When I clicked it, the gray appeared in the bottom section at (1,2).
Hmm, maybe the mechanic isn't just "2 tiles to the right." Maybe it's about the direction of the nearest adjacent green cross. Let me reconsider:
First jump: clicked green at (2,2), gray appeared at (2,4). The green at (2,3) was to the right. So the gray appeared 2 tiles to the right, in the direction of the adjacent green.
Second jump: clicked green at (2,4), gray appeared at (2,6). The green at (2,5) was to the right. So again, 2 tiles to the right.
Third attempt: clicked green at (2,6). What adjacent greens are there? The green at (3,6) is below. So maybe the gray should appear 2 tiles below? But the gray appeared at ~(30, 42) which is in the bottom section.
Let me check: 2 tiles below (2,6) would be (4,6). But the top section only has 3 rows. So (4,6) would be in the bottom section. The bottom section starts at row 30, so tile row 1 of bottom section is rows 30-33. Tile (4,6) in the overall layout... hmm, this doesn't quite work because the top and bottom sections have different layouts.
Actually, let me reconsider. The green at (2,6) in the top section is at pixel position (19, 42). The green at (3,6) is at (25, 42). They're 6 pixels apart vertically (one tile apart). Two tiles below (2,6) would be at row 30-33, which is the first row of the bottom section. The gray appeared at ~(30, 42), which is indeed in the bottom section's first row, same column.
So the mechanic might be: clicking a green cross creates a gray cross 2 tiles in the direction of the nearest adjacent green cross. If the adjacent green is to the right, the gray appears 2 tiles right. If the adjacent green is below, the gray appears 2 tiles below.
In this case, the green at (2,6) has a green at (3,6) below it. So the gray appeared 2 tiles below, which is in the bottom section at tile (1,2).
Now, if I click the gray at (30, 42), the green at (2,6) should jump over (3,6) to (1,2) in the bottom section, absorbing (3,6) in the process.
But wait - the bottom section has a green at (37, 42) which is tile (2,2). The gray is at tile (1,2) in the bottom section. So the gray is above the existing green in the bottom section.
Let me execute this jump and see what happens.
